evidence:
Grounded at frozen HEAD 3abee5a6add69443e49322e96f9130b834686235 against base 565def869ae50e47e6da7388ea333229050eaf8d. register.js:278-314 constructs contextVersion from topic revision and command epoch, deduplicates invitations only at equal contextVersion (with the partial/whole exception), then stores the entire new body. There is no supersession of a different-version non-inflight invitation. Structural trace: one passive invitation starts an append; N subsequent distinct contexts with that same id add N objects/body strings while appendInflight remains true (540-554). Alternatively each completed deny clears inflight but preserves current-run entries, sets a 30-second backoff, and performs no eviction (563-572; discardStale at 154-161 removes only lost-run items). Recovery selects every retained passive revision into frame(batch), whose map/join processes all bodies (54-60, 546-554). The 1024 cap at 336-338 bounds completed invitation identity bookkeeping, not queue entries or body bytes. Full-file inspection found queue removal at completion, attention clear, predecessor settlement and lifecycle loss; none coalesces pending invitation context versions. Thus this history lasts while the same run/session stays live and appends remain unresolved or denied; it ends on successful draining or the documented lifecycle cleanup, not an unconditional leak beyond session lifetime. The repo's existing manual-append controls at delivery.test.ts:1973-1998 and 2038-2059 already assert two same-id entries for changed/whole context while append is pending; they do not test repeated revisions.

Canonical bounds do not stop this trace: invitation_content.rs:1153-1175 resets allocation counts when the canonical context key changes, retaining one canonical item row; its Confirm retires non-control descriptors and clears the completed outbox (949-963). watch.rs:690-711 confirms after stdout write/flush, with no mod-append completion handshake. The JS stream consumer invokes cb.line synchronously and continues parsing (register.js:923-939), so a pending append provides no backpressure to those confirmations. Passive notification does not arm stall detection (mod_channels.rs:643-651); the stall predicate additionally requires an attention push and an old ordinary pending receipt (555-585; TRUST-POLICY.md:428-433), so a lone lazy invitation supplies no finite lifetime through that mechanism.

I searched the named design documents and TRUST-POLICY for queue, coalescing, latest/quiescent/transient context, supersession, append/stall, memory, downstream and limit equivalents. Accepted limits are distinct: TRUST-POLICY.md:1524-1528 accepts downstream silent loss after flush, and Q3 design:87-89 explicitly leaves queued transport frames/global transport memory outside Q3. Neither accepts newly accumulating obsolete bodies for one canonical invitation inside the mod. The invitation design:103-105 deliberately selects coalesced latest context rather than every transient revision; TRUST-POLICY.md:1554-1557 and 1658-1662 repeat that contract. Coalescing the latest non-inflight context while preserving the active append and partial-to-whole upgrade can satisfy that contract without history-sized recovery frames. This is material introduced growth and redundant model-visible context for a fixed canonical workload, not a demand for an overall queue cap or recovery during permanent failure. The base register.js:250 ignores invitation items, and 273 deduplicates accepted items solely by id; its already-unbounded queue across distinct ids does not contain this same-invitation revision history. Significant long-session memory/recovery allocation risk merits Should-fix. This verdict relies only on repository-defined conditional append/deny behavior and code structure, not an external assertion about native API timing; no external premise or runtime execution was needed.
